structure.title: Preface
structure.summary: This letter from Mahindra & Mahindra Ltd. dated 28th June 2025 is addressed to several stock exchanges and concerns compliance with SEBI Listing Regulations. It provides the Integrated Annual Report for FY 2024-25 and the Notice of the 79th Annual General Meeting (AGM) to be held on 31st July 2025 via video conferencing. The AGM agenda includes adoption of standalone and consolidated financial statements, dividend declaration, re-appointment of directors (Rajesh Jejurikar and Anand G. Mahindra), revision in remuneration to the Non-Executive Chairman, re-appointment of independent directors (Nisaba Godrej and Muthiah Murugappan), ratification of Cost Auditors' remuneration, appointment of Secretarial Auditor, and approval of material related party transactions. The documents are available via web links and are being sent electronically, with physical copies on request.

structure.title: CHAIRMAN’S MESSAGE
structure.summary: The text includes the Chairman's message, which uses Bob Dylan's quote and the Samudra Manthan metaphor to describe global flux, protectionism, trade disruptions, and opportunities for India; emphasizes resilience and Mahindra's banyan tree structure. The Group CEO & MD's message highlights FY25 financial performance (revenue ₹1,59,211 crore, PAT ₹12,929 crore), business segment growth, EV launches, sustainability initiatives (Kaabil, Nanhi Kali), awards (Company of the Year), and the 'Bold by Design' theme. It also covers the integrated report's evolution, six capitals framework, and table of contents.

structure.title: HOW TO READ THE REPORT
structure.summary: This guide explains how to read an Integrated Report focused on value creation for all stakeholders through six capitals: Financial, Manufactured, Intellectual, Human, Social and Relationship, and Natural. It describes a value creation model with KPIs and notes that statutory financial statements comply with Indian regulations (Companies Act 2013, Ind AS, SEBI LODR 2015, Secretarial Standards) and reference international frameworks (IR Framework, GRI, BRSR). It includes a forward-looking statement disclaimer, defines interchangeable terms for Mahindra & Mahindra Limited, and specifies the reporting period (1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025) and scope covering core operations across automotive, farm equipment, spares, research valley, two-wheeler, construction equipment, and powertrain divisions, plus other group businesses, aligning with National Voluntary Guidelines' nine principles.

structure.title: PERFORMANCE HIGHLIGHTS
structure.summary: Mahindra & Mahindra's FY25 performance highlights include SUV revenue market share of 22.5% (210 bps YoY increase) and LCV market share of 51.9% (290 bps increase). Consolidated income from operations rose 14% to ₹1,59,211 Cr with PAT up 15% to ₹12,929 Cr; standalone income from operations increased 17% to ₹1,18,625 Cr with PAT up 11% to ₹11,855 Cr. BEV innovation featured the launch of BE 6 and XEV 9e SUVs and a record 30,179 Day-1 bookings. Mahindra Financial Services AUM grew 17% to ₹1,19,673 Cr, Lifespaces gross development value addition was ₹18,100 Cr (4.1x YoY), Logistics revenue rose 11% to ₹6,105 Cr, Farm Equipment market share was 43.3% (170 bps increase), Electric 3-Wheelers market share was 42.9% with 4.6x volume growth in three years, Tech Mahindra EBIT margin was 9.7% (360 bps increase), Holidays added a record 520 keys (34% increase), and Susten won 2.1 GWp deals including 0.4 GWp hybrid.

It details the Group's three-phase evolution: disciplined capital allocation (focusing on market leaders, full-potential businesses, and growth gems), pivot to growth (strategies for Auto, Farm, Mahindra Finance, Tech Mahindra, and growth gems), and deliver scale (FY25 performance with 14% revenue growth, 18% ROE). structure.title: 2. ACHIEVE FULL POTENTIAL
key_items: Strategic Imperatives; Key Highlights; Achievements in FY25
structure.summary: The text highlights turnaround journeys of Mahindra Finance and Tech Mahindra. Mahindra Finance, a leading NBFC, overcame COVID-era challenges through risk-focused underwriting and tech investments, achieving GS3 below 4%, 17% AUM growth, and 1.9% ROA. Its strategic imperatives include asset quality, vehicle financing leadership, new business growth, rural housing turnaround, and digital resilience. Key highlights: 48% SME disbursement growth, insurance partnerships, and cloud migration. Tech Mahindra, a global IT services firm, embarked on a three-year turnaround targeting growth, margins, and organization. It improved EBIT margins to 9.7% and ROCE to 21.3%. Its 'Scale at Speed' strategy focuses on large deals, BFSI/Healthcare/Retail expansion, margin improvement via Project Fortius, and culture building. Key highlights: $2,680 Mn deal wins (up 43%), 4-day DSO improvement, and 85% FCF return.

nodes.title: ANNEXURE I
nodes.summary: Mahindra & Mahindra's Dividend Distribution Policy outlines principles for balancing dividend payouts and retained earnings, effective from April 1, 2016. Dividends are declared per share on Rs. 5 face value ordinary equity shares, with recommendations typically annual after full-year results and before the AGM, plus possible interim dividends. The company targets a 20-35% payout ratio of standalone PAT, considering internal factors (profits, cash flow, reserves, earnings stability, future cash needs, brand acquisitions, leverage, investments, capex, debt-equity ratio) and external factors (business cycles, economic environment, financing costs, taxes, regulatory changes, industry outlook, inflation, dividend history). Special dividends may be recommended, and lower or no dividends may be considered with rationale. Retained earnings may fund capital expenditure, growth, investments, dividends, share capitalisation, buybacks, contingencies, or capital structure correction. The policy is reviewed periodically, disclosed on the website and annual report, with 10-year dividend history in the annual report.
